      "observations": [
        "The full owned functional diff and needed accepted event receivers were read. The patch adds private touch-ID/Y-coordinate state and shares a private pixel accumulator with the existing wheel handler. A single-touch move prevents default, adds its vertical delta, requests a step when the measured first-row height is exceeded and resets the accumulator on that step. The actual subclass receivers move a week in multiweek view and a month in month view; a row-height threshold is not a universal row-distance scroll result.",
        "The end/cancel handler deletes changed touch identifiers, then tests the Map object itself with !this.#mOngoingTouches. That allocated object remains truthy when empty, so this condition does not reset the partial offset after the final touch ends, contrary to the adjacent comment. Accepted code retains this exact object-versus-size mismatch. A later gesture can therefore start with the remaining partial accumulator in this static path; no device behavior was reproduced.",
        "Multitouch moves return after preventDefault when the tracked size exceeds one. Wheel handling retains its mouse-scroll preference and modifier gate, while the new touch path has no equivalent preference/modifier test. The code does not establish pinch gestures, inertial motion, native passive-listener behavior or cross-input cleanup guarantees.",
        "There are no added tests or assertions. The comments explain accumulation and intended end-of-drag reset, but the reset comment currently states an effect that its condition does not perform. The actual .size check is the needed condition to review; no source repair or broader style rule is authorized by this study.",
        "B reads Parent's complete primary 1969263 current 0–3, activity and actual footer, and C3's full D251992 creation-to-final timeline, all nine actual current/older inline bodies and three actual replacements. Video attachment metadata is not summary history; no video pixels, Try jobs or device run are opened. The original reviewer lacked a touch device; a later UX reviewer's reported day/multiweek/month gestures remain attributed historical testing.",
        "Actual source adopts initialized private state, named private handlers, the Map<number, number> field type and separate listener registration despite older Not Done labels. The author explicitly rejects clearing the whole touch Map because another finger may remain active; the final code deletes only changed identifiers.
